reviews.title: 50/50 odds on 25 dollar packs is definitely rigged, more than you’d think.
reviews.text: I win about 1 every 12 times rather than half of the time on 50/50 odds consistently. Someone on a newer account will hit it much more often. They might track how much you’ve spent or if you’ve shipped cards. The probability of losing on 50/50 odds as much as I’ve seen is impossibly low for it to be genuine. I’ve opened over 6,000 packs and you’re much better off using max or high instead of 50/50. It’s probably 50/50 for new users to draw them in, then once they’ve either won enough or they’ve put in a lot of money, they will skew the odds, which is illegal and a scam. Remember that they’re unregulated and this app is illegal in Nevada. Not only that but the 50/50 option is banned in several states as well. They call it a card trading app instead of gambling to avoid regulation, so that they can further scam you, more than a casino can. My pull rate on 25$ packs and 50$ packs is less than 1/10 and the probability of that being genuine is low. Also every time I ship a card they give me a card saying they read each review, which is untrue, I haven’t seen a singular response to any review. I just want to know how 50/50 beyond 5 dollar packs is that rigged. I had extra to spend and I just tested this on 25’s as much as I could, but it’s designed so that you lose the 25’s then you go down to 10 and try to 50/50 on that, then you get back and lose again on 25’s every single time.

reviews.title: Good but missing features
reviews.text:
I really want to love this app and company but it’s missing some big features that make it hard. 

Pros:
• The app itself is honestly the best experience of any card ripping apps with how interactive it is. 
• The simple and clean layout of everything. 
• The ability to track cards that have been shipped to you and their current values.

Cons:
• The removal of “Steady” pack styles, which lowered the chance of a big hit but lowered the risk.
• I’ve opened nearly 6,000 packs, with most of them being the $1-$5 range, but probably 10-15% being in the $10+ packs and I rarely get any cards that are worth 1.3x what I payed. I understand the odds are what they are it still feels bad when you get a Gold, the best you can get and only a .2% chance of getting, and it’s only double what you put in.
• My biggest complaint is the shipping pricing. I’ve had over 60 cards shipped from them and each one cost me at least $6. I had 15+ shipped and delivered at the same time but I had pay individual shipping and they all were all in separate packaging. while I appreciate the how they package the cards so they don’t get damaged, the price is a big issue especially when I’ve had other companies ship 10+ cards for around $20. 

Features I’d like to see added:
• Ability to keep cards in the showroom without being forced into selling or shipping the cards
• Ability to sell and/ or auction the cards in your showroom to other people on the app.

reviews.title: A predatory psychological trap disguised as an app
reviews.text:
This app is pure evil. When you first create an account, the algorithm is completely rigged in your favor. You win nearly every single pack you open. It triggers an immediate dopamine rush, tricks you into thinking you’re lucky, and manipulates you into linking your credit card info.
But the moment they have you hooked, the win rates drop off a cliff to zero, and you can’t hit anything to save your life. They deliberately bait you into chasing that initial high, draining your bank account while feeding you nothing but garbage.
To show you exactly how sick and predatory their mindset is: they set my DEFAULT profile picture to that meme of the miner turning around right before hitting diamonds, captioned "99% of gamblers quit before they win big." Insane. They are actively weaponizing gambling addiction tropes and the sunk-cost fallacy against their own users to keep them spending.
This isn't a game or a card app; it is a calculated financial parasite designed to extract money from you through deep psychological manipulation. I deleted my account and cut my losses. Stay far away from this garbage.

reviews.title: Fun at first, but an expensive disappointment
reviews.text:
I spent approximately $140 on Rips by Triumph and opened 174 packs. My highest-valued pull was about $65, and after repeatedly selling cards back to try for a bigger pull, I ultimately came away with no cards I was happy to keep.

I pulled gold cards from the $25, $10, and $5 packs, and every one was valued well below the price I paid for the pack it came from. Even getting a gold card repeatedly left me disappointed with the value I received.

What started as entertainment became a frustrating cycle of opening packs, selling the results, and hoping the next opening would finally make the experience worthwhile. It became far too easy to keep putting money and the value of previous pulls back into that cycle. I was left feeling that every disappointing result came with the temptation to spend again.

The higher-value cards I encountered were also Japanese versions, which did not match what I was hoping to collect. That added to my disappointment with the overall experience.

I understand that opening packs involves chance and that valuable cards are not guaranteed. My concern is how quickly the excitement turned into chasing a better result, with very little satisfaction to show for the money spent.

After spending $140 and opening 174 packs, I left deeply disappointed and regretting the purchase. Based on my experience, I cannot recommend this app.

This review won’t be seen by people on the app either unfortunately. They only show the positive reviews it seems. I could have over $1000 worth of cards but all I have coming to me is a $30 card because I didn’t understand that it auto sells after 6 or 7 days. That’s unfair. reviews.title: Brutal hit rates but awesome concept.
reviews.text: Started off solid, on my first deposit hit a $109 profit on $100 pack opening. Have deposited 1K since opening that card and have opened many $25 / $50 / $100 packs and a $250 pack since. Totaling 683 pack openings altogether. I don’t need to necessarily profit but only seem to hit golds and reds on the $1-$5 pack openings and the profit is never huge just a few dollars here and there on the hits. The idea of this app is pretty cool and the presentation is great. I do understand it’s gambling at the end of the day but the odds and algorithm seem extremely scammy to me. Just doesn’t seem like there’s any actual chance to profit or for huge hits, Mainly a double up on your bigger hits at most, unless you cash out or ship the one decent sized win you typically receive after a first deposit. I would recommend buying the cards you’re interested in at market price. Awesome concept, just extremely tilted in the houses direction with very little to zero chances of breaking even or coming away with any “big” hits. The bonus card feature is cool but it’s few and far between on it working in the players favor. I’d say roughly 20% of my bonus card rips have even accumulated to the price of the actual pack I have paid to open. Again, it’s an awesome idea and concept, the cards I’ve shipped came within a week which was nice. The presentation is great. Just wouldn’t recommend it to anyone that doesn’t want to get rinsed.

reviews.title: The house always wins
reviews.text:
This app isn’t a scam, but it is designed heavily to encourage gambling and to discourage actually taking home any cards.  The buy back prices they have are almost always too high to justify shipping the raw cards, especially since they don’t combine shipping.  It’s 5.50 per card, so pretty much all the cards in the lower tiers you would want to sell back whether it’s a card you would have wanted or not.  It makes more sense to just go buy it elsewhere and have it sent for .50, or maybe even free.  

The wins are usually very minor and don’t make up for the crashing losses, so even on tiers with more generous odds you will still most likely find your money gradually eroded away without winning anything worth shipping.   

I encountered maybe 2 slabs in my unwise gambling venture, and they were cards I was surprised someone would bother having graded.  Overall if you enjoy gambling and want to most likely blow all your money then whatever.  But if you actually want some cards I would look elsewhere.

reviews.title: They let you win at first then quit
reviews.text: I’ve been using the app for a few weeks now and have put in or pulled out money daily since then. At first everything the odds seemed legit and while I wasn’t in profit, it seemed fair to what was stated (I do the max odds that have a 10% chance of a grail) and my friend was doing the same thing with roughly the same result he was just in slight profit because of one lucky win. Then I noticed a dry spell and started to get suspicious so I tallied up all the packs I had bought without hitting a grail. It was exactly 17 $25 packs and if I were to guess probably about 30 $10 packs. That’s nearly 50 packs that each have a 10% chance and not a single thing. I mentioned that to my friend and he said his was the same way so I asked him to go and look at how many times he’d put in money. He told me he opened 11 $25 and also roughly double that in $10 without a single hit. If you know anything about stats the larger the pool the less skewed the results will be. In a pool of 80 each with a 10% chance it falls out of the “bad luck” area and is clear there is some sort of altercations to the odds after they’ve got you hooked. From what I’ve heard this is a common problem with gambling apps and websites, I just figured triumph was big enough that they didn’t need to. It’s a shame because I actually really liked the app and have even had a few cards sent to myself.

Their ads are ridiculous showing people pull HUGE grail hits off of cheap packs.. I get it, they’re ads, but still… and I dont  know why I’m even calling them packs, you get one card per “rip”. You’d probably have better luck scattering a bunch of cards on a table front side down and picking one at random. This app targets people who are dopamine addicts and can’t get enough of that “maybe this time I’ll hit” rush they get, and RIPS targets that population set predatorily. Also, if you want to keep some of the cards and have them shipped to you, they force you to pay the $5-$6 shipping per card and there is no option to send them all at once. Don’t waste your time or money with this garbage app and others like it. Go to a local card shop or trusted online source, and pick out the cards you actually want and pay only what the card currently comps for or less if you can. You’ll save yourself the headache and you’ll save a bunch of $$$. This was just an experiment for me, and the experiment is over and the results are in: download this app if you want to get RIPPED OFF!

reviews.title: Fun App, but beware if you get an expensive card
reviews.text: I’ve spent a lot of money on this app, and for the most part have been very satisfied. It got to a place where I had accumulated some cash on here, and decided to open one of the more expensive packs. I opened a card worth around $875, and had it shipped - I was so excited. I’ve had 7 cards shipped without issue, so I had built some trust in the app. In this case, I had this card shipped with 2 others at the same time (all separate shipments). I have since received the other 2, but not this one. The card was due to be delivered 4 days ago (per USPS tracking #). I can’t get in touch with anyone from support - the AI chat bot keeps ending the chat or not responding. reviews.title: Verification pending
reviews.text:
I honestly cannot recommend this app based on my experience. I currently have over $100 worth of cards and rips in my account, but my identity verification has been pending for several months with no resolution. Because of this, I am unable to cash out my funds or have my cards shipped when I need them.
I have contacted customer support multiple times, but the responses are extremely slow, typically only once per day, and most of the communication appears to come from an AI-based support system that has not been helpful in resolving my issue. Despite providing the information requested, my verification status remains unchanged.
The support team informed me that my ID information must match my account preferences, but there are no clear options within the app to update or correct those details on my own. Instead, users are required to go through support, which has made the process even more frustrating and time-consuming.
As a result, I have had over $100 tied up in my account for months without access to my funds or assets. From a customer perspective, this feels extremely unfair and has left me feeling misled by the platform.
My advice to anyone considering this app is to complete and confirm identity verification before depositing money or making purchases. Otherwise, you may risk having your account stuck in pending status for an extended period of time, with limited support available to help resolve the issue.

reviews.title: What To Expect
reviews.text: I got this app super excited to rip packs but in reality it’s not what you expect. First off, I’ve opened 250 packs and haven’t even landed a card worth more than $12. The packs I’ve opened were $1,$5$,10,$25. You have to understand this is completely gambling and quite honestly seems like a bit of a scam. For example, if I open a pack that’s $5 and I actually get a decent card, it’s likely only worth $6-$7 at most which is then followed by 3-4 straight $1 cards. Money dwindles quickly here because it’s not designed for you to win. The odds of you getting a card higher than the value of the pack you buy is allegedly 40%, but I’d love to see the actual stats because in my case it was more like 5-10%. In theory, this seems like a great app and I was honestly super excited about it, but it seems like a scam to me. As long as you’re comfortable gambling here, and more than likely ending up like me and losing, then you’ll enjoy this app. Otherwise, stay away, you might as well go to a casino and as we all know; the house always wins. Disappointed overall.

reviews.title: Takes Your Money Instantly — Won’t Let You Get Anything Back
reviews.text:
The concept is straightforward and the pack-opening experience works fine, but the app has a serious and apparently intentional flaw: you cannot withdraw your account balance or request card shipments under any circumstances. Every attempt to do either results in links that simply never load — no error, no spinner, nothing. Meanwhile, the deposit and purchase functions work flawlessly every single time.
The vault system compounds the problem. Cards are held for seven days and then repurchased by the platform on their terms if you haven’t acted — which is difficult to do when the action buttons don’t function. You’re left in a loop where money flows in freely but cannot leave by any means, whether as a cash withdrawal or a physical card shipment.
This isn’t a bug. A legitimate platform doesn’t selectively break only the features that send value back to the customer. Until withdrawals and shipments are fully functional and verifiable, I cannot recommend this app to anyone. One star.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
